label: words
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: roof
Length: 30 s: 95-120 words in all, one sentence per beat (11 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 108 words in all, about 10 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 120 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- One inch of rain on a 1,000 square foot roof is over 600 gallons of water.
- Asphalt shingles are the most common roofing material on US homes
- Shingles are laid from the bottom edge up, each row overlapping the one below.

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: four posts and a flat board appear. actions: roof show (on "board")
   idea: a flat board on four posts keeps the sky off you
   cue words: "board"
2. problem
   on screen: rain pools on the flat board and drips below. actions: light storm (on "But"); rain start (on "But"); pool flood (on "pools"); drip start (on "drips")
   idea: rain pools on the flat top and drips through
   cue words: "But", "pools", "drips"
3. fix1
   on screen: the board halves swing up into two slopes and the water runs off. actions: drip stop (on "So"); pool drain (on "tilt"); roof tilt (on "tilt")
   idea: tilt it into two slopes so the rain runs off
   cue words: "So", "tilt"
4. problem2
   on screen: water pours off both eaves and puddles spread with splashes. actions: sheet 5 start (on "pours"); sheet 4 start (on "pours"); sheet 3 start (on "pours"); sheet 2 start (on "pours"); sheet 1 start (on "pours"); sheet 0 start (on "pours"); puddles rise (on "pours"); splash start (on "mud")
   idea: now all that water pours off the edge and splashes mud everywhere
   cue words: "pours", "mud"
5. fix2
   on screen: a gutter appears along the edge and a downspout carries the water down. actions: roof gutter (on "gutter"); splash stop (on "gutter"); puddles dry (on "downspout"); spout grow (on "downspout"); spout flow show (on "downspout"); sheet 0 stop (on "gutter"); sheet 1 stop (on "gutter"); sheet 2 stop (on "gutter"); sheet 3 stop (on "gutter"); sheet 4 stop (on "gutter"); sheet 5 stop (on "gutter")
   idea: a gutter catches it and a downspout carries it down
   cue words: "gutter", "downspout"
6. problem3
   on screen: drips fall through the gaps in the boards. actions: drip 2 start (on "seeps"); drip start (on "gaps")
   idea: rain still seeps through the gaps between the boards
   cue words: "seeps", "gaps"
7. fix3
   on screen: overlapping rows of shingles appear on both slopes and the drips stop. actions: roof shingle (on "shingles"); drip 2 stop (on "shingles"); drip stop (on "shingles")
   idea: overlapping shingles shed each drop onto the one below
   cue words: "shingles"
   its fact: Asphalt shingles are the most common roofing material on US homes; Shingles are laid from the bottom edge up, each row overlapping the one below.
8. name
   on screen: an outline traces the roof. actions: roof outline show (on "pitched")
   idea: this is a pitched roof
   cue words: "pitched"
9. fact
   on screen: a gallons counter beside the roof ticks up to 600 while water runs down the downspout. actions: roof outline hide (on "inch"); rain arrows show (on "inch"); stand show (on "inch"); gallons show (on "inch"); gallons count (on "600")
   idea: one inch of rain on an ordinary roof is over 600 gallons
   cue words: "inch", "600"
   its fact: One inch of rain on a 1,000 square foot roof is over 600 gallons of water.
10. finish
   on screen: a ridge cap and a chimney appear, the rain stops. actions: gallons hide (on "Add"); rain arrows hide (on "Add"); rain stop (on "Add"); light clear (on "Add"); spout flow hide (on "Add"); roof cap (on "cap"); roof chimney (on "chimney")
   idea: a ridge cap over the top and a chimney
   cue words: "Add", "cap", "chimney"
11. congrats
   on screen: the finished roof stands calm in the sun
   idea: you have built a roof
   cue words: (none)
